claim_findings.passage: by historical standards, investment banking fees were fine, but they weren't at sort of super peak levels. So, they had some room to come up a little bit.
claim_findings.evidence: The claim sets period '3 months to 30 Jun 2026' and status 'reported'. Read in the full seg-0008 context, the sentence is a comparison against historical standards with no period of its own, and the past tense ('were fine', 'had some room to come up') most plausibly describes the level entering the quarter, which is how Barnum explains why fees rose. Attaching a quarter-specific period to a purely comparative opinion fixes a period the quote does not fix, and it is the claim the upside case in section 6 leans on for forward headroom.
claim_findings.recommendation: Drop the period field on this claim, or keep it and add a second claim capturing the sustainability framing of the surrounding answer so the upside case does not rest on a tense-ambiguous sentence alone.

outlook_findings.passage: Separately, the firm increased the equity allocation to the CIB during the quarter [claim-053] — on management's own characterisation of that same passage, a movement of equity between pockets of the one company [claim-054] rather than a group capital outflow.
outlook_findings.evidence: claim-054's own claim_text attaches 'left pocket, right pocket at the level of the company' to the roughly $150 million of Markets NII that is not offset in the bottom line, not to the equity transfer itself. Reading seg-0021 in full, Barnum's 'left pocket, right pocket' does plausibly cover the whole internal reallocation, and the phrase is present in claim-054's quote, so the brief is not citing a claim that lacks the words. But the sentence the brief builds is about the equity movement, and the sentence in the transcript that actually states that ('the consequence of that is to move some equity essentially out of Corporate into the CIB') was never extracted as a claim.
outlook_findings.recommendation: Extract the 'move some equity essentially out of Corporate into the CIB' sentence from seg-0021 as its own claim and cite that here, or reword so the internal-reallocation reading is presented as the brief's own interpretation of claim-053 rather than as management's characterisation.

outlook_findings.passage: **Investment banking fee growth relative to peers** — JPMorganChase's 30% [claim-012] against Bank of America's 50% [claim-065] is the clearest competitive signal in this evidence [claim-073].

A growth-rate gap off unequal and partly unknown bases supports a weaker conclusion than 'the clearest competitive signal in this evidence'. Section 5 handles the same comparison more carefully, calling it 'genuinely awkward'; section 8 does not carry the caveat across.
outlook_findings.recommendation: Add the base-size caveat to the monitor bullet, noting that no dollar figure for the firm's own investment banking fees is available in this evidence, so the comparison is rate-only.

outlook_findings.passage: **Peer results were same-day, not prior.** The four peer sources used here were published on the day of the call (each is dated 14 July 2026 in the archived source).

But claim-073, which the brief cites twice, also rests on claim-061 for its assertion that 'Goldman Sachs reported faster fee growth still'. claim-061 comes from a fifth same-day source, a Reuters article, whose Goldman Sachs 55% fee-growth figure never appears in the brief body or the evidence appendix. outlook_findings.recommendation: Either state the Goldman Sachs fee-growth figure in the brief with claim-061 cited and its source listed in the appendix, or drop the 'Goldman Sachs reported faster fee growth still' leg from how claim-073 is used.

The findings are: the section 4 sentence describing the CIB equity transfer as a movement 'between pockets of the one company' cites claim-054, whose own text attaches that phrase to the $150 million of Markets NII rather than to the equity transfer, and the transcript sentence that does state the equity transfer was never extracted; the section 8 peer bullet calls a 30%-versus-50% investment banking fee growth gap 'the clearest competitive signal in this evidence' without noting that the two rates sit on very different and partly unknown bases; section 9's statement that four peer sources were used omits a fifth same-day source that supplies the Goldman Sachs fee-growth leg of claim-073; and claim-032, the CEO's own 'getting close to as good as it gets' line, is extracted but cited nowhere, leaving the brief resting its normalisation premise on the narrower equities-specific caution in claims 030 and 031. Against that, the run is strong where it matters most. Every claim-### citation in the brief was opened and read, and each resolves to the right claim for its sentence; no adjacent-but-wrong citation was found. The exhaustive numeric semantic review over all value-bearing claims, including the single calculation block, found no operand, unit, sign, scope or period error, and the first-half versus full-year distinctions in the expense discussion are labelled correctly throughout. The transcript's '(sic) [Excluding]' correction is resolved the right way and is consistent with the SEC 10-Q facts. Temporal integrity holds: the only consensus source predates the event by five days, the two archived sources whose provider metadata looked clean but whose content contained post-event actuals were correctly excluded and that exclusion is disclosed, and the same-day nature of the peer results is stated rather than hidden. Both deterministic gates passed with zero issues across three attempts and the injection scan is clean.
proposed_lessons: Give a period only to claims whose quote actually fixes one; a comparison against historical standards or a general characterisation should carry no period rather than inherit the reporting quarter's.
